newsitem.title: USA: Home Depot to open 1st non-N.America store.
newsitem.headline: Home Depot to open 1st non-N.America store.

text.p: Home Depot Inc said on Thursday that it had formalized a venture under which it plans to open it first store outside of North America.

After considering Asia, Europe and Mexico, the company decided on Santiago, Chile, as the site for its first store outside the United States and Canada, and entered a joint venture with S.A.C.I. Falabella, a Chilean department store retailer, a company spokesman said.
Home Depot said it is on schedule to open the store in 1998.
America's largest home improvement retailer, Home Depot controls a 66.67 percent share of the venture with Falabella.

"The alliance with Falabella will enhance Home Depot's entry in the Chilean market, through an established credit card program, real estate opportunities, as well as assistance with systems and distribution logistics," Home Depot said in a statement. In addition, the home improvement retailer said its venture in Chile would "serve as a platform for Home Depot's growth into other Latin American countries."
Founded in 1978, Home Depot has 543 stores operating in the United States and Canada, with 1996 sales of $19.5 billion, the company said.
